Rashi on Kiddushin 53b:1:1.hebrew: ולאו ממילא שמעת מינה - בתמיה: מדכתיב: "קדש ישראל לה' ראשית תבואתו" — כתרומה הם לו, וש"מ תרומה נמי הויא קדש לה':
Rashi on Kiddushin 53b:1:1.english: And do you not understand it by itself from it? - [This is asked] in astonishment: Since it is written: “Israel is holy to the Lord, the first of His increase” — they are like teruma to Him, and learn from this that teruma also is holy to the Lord.

Rashi on Kiddushin 53b:1:2.hebrew: אמר קרא - גבי מעשר: ״לה' הוא״ — בהווייתו יהא לה':
Rashi on Kiddushin 53b:1:2.english: The verse states - With regard to tithe, “It is the Lord’s” — in its [existing] state it shall be the Lord’s.

Rashi on Kiddushin 53b:2:1.hebrew: שמעית מיניה דר' יוחנן תרתי - טעמא דמתרתי בבי דמתני', דקתני בה "בשוגג לא קידש": שגגת מעשר לר' יהודה — הואיל ואית ליה מעשר ממון הדיוט הוא, אמאי בשוגג לא קידש? ושגגת הקדש לר"מ — כיון דאית ליה במזיד קידש, שוגג מאי שנא?:
Rashi on Kiddushin 53b:2:1.english: I learned two [rulings] from Rabbi Yoḥanan - [He learned] the reason for the two clauses of the Mishnah wherein it teaches, "[If done] unwittingly, she is not betrothed": an unwitting error regarding [second] tithe according to Rabbi Yehuda — since he holds that [second] tithe is ordinary property, why is she not betrothed [if he did so] unwittingly? And an unwitting error regarding consecrated property according to Rabbi Meir — since he holds that if [done] intentionally she is betrothed, why is [doing so] unwittingly any different?

Rashi on Kiddushin 53b:2:2.hebrew: ושניהם אין אשה מתקדשת בהן - כלומר, שמעית מר' יוחנן טעמא דתרתי בבי דמתני' דאיירי בשגגות, ותני תנא דידן בתרוייהו: אין אשה מתקדשת בהן:
Rashi on Kiddushin 53b:2:2.english: And [in] both of them a woman is not betrothed with them - That is to say: I heard from Rabbi Yoḥanan the reason for the two clauses of the Mishnah that deal with unwitting [transgressions], and our Tanna taught concerning both of them: A woman is not betrothed with them.

Rashi on Kiddushin 53b:3:1.hebrew: חדא לפי שאין אשה רוצה - בחדא מינייהו פירש: לפי שאין אשה רוצה — אם היתה יודעת שהוא כן, לא קבלתו לשם קידושין, והוו להו קידושי טעות:
Rashi on Kiddushin 53b:3:1.english: One [is] because the woman does not want - Regarding one of them, he explained: "Because the woman does not want" — if she had known that it was so, she would not have accepted it for the purpose of betrothal, and it is a mistaken betrothal.

Rashi on Kiddushin 53b:3:2.hebrew: וחדא לפי שאין שניהם רוצים - דנפקא מינה, דבההיא דפריש בה ר' יוחנן "לפי שאין אשה רוצה", אם בדקנוה ואמרה "רוצה אני" ואינה מקפדת — אין אנו צריכין לבדוק אותו, דמסתמא מינח ניחא ליה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 53b:3:2.english: And the other [is] because neither of them wants [it] - For the practical difference is that in that [case] where Rabbi Yochanan explained "because the woman does not want [it]," if we inquired of her and she said, "I want [it]," and does not mind, we do not need to inquire of him, for presumptively it is satisfactory to him.

Rashi on Kiddushin 53b:3:3.hebrew: ולא ידענא הי מינייהו - באיזה מהן תלה באשה, ואיזו תלה בשניהם:
Rashi on Kiddushin 53b:3:3.english: And I do not know which of them - In which of them he made [it] dependent on the woman, and which he made dependent on both of them.

Rashi on Kiddushin 53b:3:4.english: Due to the trouble of the journey - To require her to bring it up to Jerusalem.

Rashi on Kiddushin 53b:3:5.english: By itself - For free, without effort.

Rashi on Kiddushin 53b:3:6.hebrew: דניתחיל הקדש על ידייהו - שהוא דבר איסור, וקראן הכתוב מועלי מעל. ואם קידושין הן — הרי נתחלל, שזו היא הוצאתו, כשהוציאו מרשות גבוה ונתנו לה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 53b:3:6.english: That consecrated [property] be desacralized through them - For it is a forbidden matter, and Scripture called them "those who commit a trespass." And if it is a [valid] betrothal, behold, it becomes desacralized, for this constitutes its removal [from sacred ownership], when he removed it from the domain of the Most High and gave it to her.

Rashi on Kiddushin 53b:4:1.hebrew: ור' יעקב - דאמר ״לא ידעינן הי מינייהו״, אמר לך: אטו איפכא נמי מי ליכא לפרושי, ולמימר במעשר לפי שאין שניהן רוצים, ובהקדש לפי שאין אשה רוצה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 53b:4:1.english: And Rabbi Ya’akov - [Rabbi Ya’akov,] who said, “We do not know which of them [is which],” says to you: Is it not also possible to explain the opposite, and say regarding [second] tithe [that it is] because neither of them wants [it], and regarding consecrated property [that it is] because the woman does not want [it]?

Rashi on Kiddushin 53b:4:2.english: Due to the trouble of the journey - To require her to bring it up to Jerusalem.

Rashi on Kiddushin 53b:4:3.hebrew: משום אונסא דאורחא - דעל כרחך אונסא דאורחא עליה רמיא, שהמעשר אין בו כאן שוה פרוטה, שלא ניתן להוציאו אלא בירושלים, שאפי' תמכרנו דמיו נתפסין בקדושתו, וקידושיה צריכין שיהו שוה פרוטה. הילכך, אי הוה ידע מעיקרא דמעשר הוא, כיון דבעי לקבולי עליה אונסא דאורחא, לא הוה מקדשה לה ביה, דשכיח לאיתנוסי טפי גבי איתתא מגברא. א"נ, לא רמי אחריות עליה — לא ניחא ליה דליתניס מינה, פן תיעצב ותאמר לו: קידשתני בדבר שלא נהניתי בו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 53b:4:3.english: Due to an accident along the way - For perforce [liability for] an accident along the way is cast upon him, because [second] tithe does not have the value of a peruta here, as it cannot be spent except in Jerusalem, for even if she were to sell it, its proceeds would be seized by its sanctity, and her betrothal [money] must have the value of a peruta. Therefore, had he known from the outset that it was [second] tithe, since he would have had to accept upon himself [the liability for] an accident along the way, he would not have betrothed her with it, as an accident is more common in the possession of a woman than that of a man. Alternatively, [even if] liability is not cast upon him, it is not satisfactory to him that it suffer an accident while with her, lest she become distressed and say to him: 'You betrothed me with something from which I derived no benefit.'

Rashi on Kiddushin 53b:4:4.hebrew: בשלמא איהי לא ניחא לה דניתחל הקדש על ידה - דמה הנאה יש לה בחילולו? אם לא תקבלנו, יצטרך זה לקדשה בהיתר משלו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 53b:4:4.english: Granted, [as for] her, it is not satisfactory to her that consecrated [property] be desacralized through her - For what benefit does she have in its desacralization? If she does not accept it, this [man] will have to betroth her with permitted [property] of his own.

Rashi on Kiddushin 53b:4:5.hebrew: דניקני איתתא ממילא - ואע"פ שעליו לשלם להקדש, השתא מיהא ניחא ליה, שמא אין לו משלו עכשיו כלום:
Rashi on Kiddushin 53b:4:5.english: That he acquire a woman by itself - And even though he must pay the Temple treasury, for now at least it is satisfactory to him, as perhaps he currently has nothing of his own.

Rashi on Kiddushin 53b:5:1.english: A woman - We have already stated that she is not betrothed in [a case of] unwitting [use of] consecrated property according to Rabbi Meir.

Rashi on Kiddushin 53b:5:2.hebrew: מעות מהו שיצאו לחולין - להנות מהן עתה, וזה יתחייב בהן קרבן מעילה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 53b:5:2.english: What is [the law regarding whether] the money becomes desacralized - [So as to permit her] to derive benefit from them now, and this [man] will become liable on their account for a sacrilege offering.

Rashi on Kiddushin 53b:5:3.hebrew: היאך יצאו לחולין - במה יצאו מרשות הקדש, אחרי שאין דבריהם קיימין:
Rashi on Kiddushin 53b:5:3.english: How can they become desacralized - By what means would they leave the domain of the sanctuary, since their words are not binding?

Rashi on Kiddushin 53b:6:1.hebrew: במכר מאי - לקח החפץ במעות הקדש בשוגג, לרבי מאיר: קנה או לא קנה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 53b:6:1.english: With regard to a sale, what [is the law]? - [If] he purchased the item with consecrated money unwittingly, according to Rabbi Meir: Did he acquire [it] or not acquire [it]?

Rashi on Kiddushin 53b:6:2.hebrew: לא קנה - ולא יצאו מעות לחולין. ואין מעילה לרבי מאיר בהקדשות אלא באוכל אוכלי הקדש, אבל המוציא מעות הקדש — אין לו מעילה; בכל מקום שהן, שם הקדש עליהם:
Rashi on Kiddushin 53b:6:2.english: He does not acquire [it] - And the money does not become desacralized. And according to Rabbi Meir, there is no [liability for] misuse of consecrated property regarding consecrated items except for one who eats food of consecrated items, but one who spends consecrated money does not incur [liability for] misuse; wherever they are, the status of consecrated property remains upon them.

Rashi on Kiddushin 53b:7:1.hebrew: חנוני כבעל הבית - משנה היא במעילה: גזבר המפקיד מעות אצל שולחני — אם צרורין, לא ישתמש בהם; לפיכך אם הוציא, לא מעל הגזבר אלא שולחני. ואם מותרים, ישתמש בהם; לפיכך אם הוציא, מעל הגזבר, דברשותיה עבד, דמידע ידע דשולחני צריך למעות תדיר. אבל בעה"ב, בין כך ובין כך לא ישתמש בהן, דלאו אדעתא דהכי אפקדינהו גביה, דסתם בעה"ב אינו משתמש תמיד במעות; לפיכך אם הוציא, מעל בעה"ב, ולא הגזבר שהפקידו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 53b:7:1.english: A storekeeper is like a homeowner - It is a Mishnah in [tractate] Meilah: [Regarding] a treasurer who deposits [consecrated] coins with a money changer: if they are tied up [in a bundle], he may not use them; therefore, if he spent [them], the treasurer has not committed misuse [of consecrated property], but rather the money changer [has]. And if they are loose, he may use them; therefore, if he spent [them], the treasurer has committed misuse, because he acted with his permission, as [the treasurer] well knows that a money changer constantly needs coins. But [with] a homeowner, in either case he may not use them, for it was not with this in mind that he deposited them with him, as an ordinary homeowner does not constantly use coins; therefore, if he spent [them], the homeowner has committed misuse, and not the treasurer who deposited them.

Rashi on Kiddushin 53b:7:2.hebrew: חנוני כבעה"ב - שאינו צריך תמיד למעות, שנותנים לו פירות, וכל מכר חנותם באשראי, ודי לו במיעוט מעות שבידו. ר' יהודה אומר: חנוני כשולחני:
Rashi on Kiddushin 53b:7:2.english: A shopkeeper is like a homeowner - For he does not constantly need money, as they give him produce and all sales of their shop are on credit, and the small amount of money in his possession is sufficient for him. [Whereas] Rabbi Yehuda says: A shopkeeper is like a moneychanger.

Rashi on Kiddushin 53b:8:1.hebrew: אבל דכ"ע - המוציא מעות הקדש, מעל אחד מהם. אלמא, במכר לר' מאיר קנה, דאם לא קנה — היאך יצאו מעות לחולין:
Rashi on Kiddushin 53b:8:1.english: But everyone [agrees] - [When] one spends consecrated money, one of them has committed me'ilah. This implies that in [a case of] a sale, according to Rabbi Meir [the buyer] has acquired [it]; for if he did not acquire [it], how did the money become secular?

Rashi on Kiddushin 53b:8:2.hebrew: לדידי - אם הוציא, לא מעל לא זה ולא זה, שאין מעילה במעות אלא באוכלין:
Rashi on Kiddushin 53b:8:2.english: According to me - If he spent [the money], neither this [one] nor that [one] has misused consecrated property, for there is no misuse of consecrated property with coins, but only with food items.

Rashi on Kiddushin 53b:8:3.english: According to you - Who hold that there is misuse [of consecrated property] with coins:

Rashi on Kiddushin 53b:8:4.hebrew: אודי לי מיהא דחנוני כבעה"ב - והוא מעל ולא גזבר, דלאו ברשותיה עבד. וא"ל ר' יהודה: לא מודינא לך בהא, אלא כשולחני הוא, ומעל גזבר — דמידע ידע דצריך תמיד למעות לקנות סחורה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 53b:8:4.english: Concede to me at least that a storekeeper is like a homeowner - and [therefore] he has committed me'ilah, and not the treasurer, for he did not act with his authorization. And Rabbi Yehuda said to him: I do not concede to you on this; rather, he is like a moneychanger, and the treasurer has committed me'ilah, for [the treasurer] well knew that [the storekeeper] constantly needs money to buy merchandise.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 53b:4:1.hebrew: איהו לא ניחא ליה משום אונסא דאורחא - פי' בקונטרס: דעל כרחך אונסא דאורחא עליה דידיה רמיא, שהמעשר אין כאן בו שוה פרוטה, שלא ניתן להוציאו אלא בירושלים — שאפי' ימכרנו, דמיו נתפסין בקדושתו, וקידושין צריכין שיהו שוים שוה פרוטה. הילכך, אי הוה ידע מעיקרא דמעשר הוי, כיון דבעי לקבולי עליה אונסא דאורחא לא הוה מקדש לה ביה, דשכיח לאיתנוסי גבי איתתא טפי מגברא. משמע מתוך פירושו, שלא יחולו הקידושין במזיד עד שיהו בירושלים. וקשה, דפריך בבכורות (דף ט:): "והרי מעשר שהקפידה תורה בכסף צורה" — פי': כשפודה אותו, צריך לפדותו בכסף שיש בו צורה — "וקאמר ר' יהודה: במזיד קידש!" ומאי פריך? והא איהו לא אמר שיגמרו עד שיהיה המעשר בירושלים, ואירושלים לא הקפידה תורה בכסף צורה, דכתיב (דברים יד): "ונתת הכסף בכל אשר תאוה נפשך"! אלא ש"מ: מקודשת אפי' בגבולין אם קבלה את המעשר. לכן נ"ל כפירוש הקונטרס שני, דפירש: אי נמי, אפי' דאין אחריות מוטל עליו, לא ניחא ליה דתיהוי לה תרעומת עליה לומר לו: "קדשתני בדבר שלא הועיל לי". מיהו קשה, דמשמע הכא דמתני' איירי בגבולין, ואפ"ה קאמר ר' יהודה דבמזיד קידש, דמעשר ממון הדיוט הוא. וכן משמע לקמן (קידושין דף נד:), דקאמר: "הפודה מעשר שני שלו מוסיף חומש", ומוקי לה כר' יהודה; וההיא ע"כ בגבולין איירי, דאי בירושלים — אין פודין בו מעשר שני; אלמא משמע דמעשר שני ממון הדיוט הוא לר' יהודה אפי' בגבולין. וקשה מפרק חלק (סנהדרין דף קיב:), דמשמע התם דבגבולין כ"ע לא פליגי דממון גבוה: גבי עיסת מעשר שני, ר"מ פוטר מן החלה וחכמים מחייבין, ואמר רב חסדא: מחלוקת במעשר שני בירושלים, דר"מ סבר ממון גבוה הוא, ורבנן סברי ממון הדיוט הוא; אבל בגבולין — דברי הכל פטורים! וי"ל: דאע"ג דלר' יהודה ממון הדיוט הוא אפי' בגבולין, מ"מ קאמר רב חסדא דלאו עיסה היא להתחייב בחלה, הואיל ואין ראויה שם לאכול:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 53b:4:1.english: "For him it is not satisfactory due to mishaps along the way" - The Kuntres explained that perforce the mishap of the journey falls upon him, because the [second] tithe is not worth a perutah here [outside Jerusalem], as it cannot be spent anywhere except in Jerusalem — for even if he sells it, its proceeds are seized with its sanctity, and betrothal requires [the item] to be worth a perutah. Therefore, had he known from the beginning that it was second tithe, since he would have to accept upon himself [responsibility for] mishaps of the journey, he would not have betrothed her with it, because mishaps are more likely to occur in the possession of a woman than in the possession of a man. It is implied from his explanation that [even] when done intentionally, the betrothal would not take effect until they are in Jerusalem. And this is difficult, for [the Gemara] objects in Bekhorot (9b): "Yet is there not [second] tithe, regarding which the Torah was particular [that it be redeemed only] with minted coin" — meaning, when one redeems it, one must redeem it with coins that have an emblem — "and Rabbi Yehudah says that [if he betrothed her with it] intentionally, she is betrothed!" And what was [the Gemara's] objection? Surely he did not intend for [the betrothal] to be completed until the second tithe is in Jerusalem, and as for Jerusalem, the Torah was not particular about minted coin, as it is written (Deuteronomy 14[:26]): "And you shall spend the money for whatever your soul desires"! Rather, conclude from this that she is betrothed even in the provinces if she accepted the second tithe. Therefore, it seems to me like the Kuntres's second explanation, which explained: Alternatively, even though liability is not incumbent upon him, it is not satisfactory to him that she should have a grievance against him, saying to him, "You betrothed me with something that brought me no benefit." However, this is difficult: for it implies here that our Mishnah is dealing with [betrothal in] the provinces, and even so Rabbi Yehudah says that [if he betrothed her] intentionally she is betrothed, because second tithe is personal property. And it is similarly implied below (Kiddushin 54b), where [the Mishnah] states: "One who redeems his own second tithe adds a fifth," and [the Gemara] establishes it according to Rabbi Yehudah; and that [case] perforce deals with [redemption in] the provinces, for in Jerusalem one does not redeem second tithe. Thus, it implies that second tithe is personal property according to Rabbi Yehudah even in the provinces. And this is difficult from the chapter [entitled] Chelek (Sanhedrin 112b), where it implies there that in the provinces, everyone agrees that it is property of the Most High: regarding dough of second tithe, Rabbi Meir exempts [it] from challah and the Sages obligate [it], and Rav Ḥisda said: Their dispute is regarding second tithe in Jerusalem, for Rabbi Meir maintains it is property of the Most High and the Rabbis maintain it is personal property; but in the provinces, all agree that it is exempt! And it can be answered: Even though according to Rabbi Yehudah it is personal property even in the provinces, nevertheless Rav Ḥisda said that it is not considered "dough" to be obligated in challah, since it is not fit to be eaten there.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 53b:6:1.hebrew: אף במכר לא קנה - ולא יצאו מעות לחולין. ואין מעילה לר"מ אלא באוכל הקדש, אבל במוציא הקדש אין לו מעילה, דכל מקום שהוא — שם הקדש חל עליו, דכל היכא דאיתא — בי גזא דרחמנא איתיה, כיון דאי הוה ידע לא הוה מפיק. אבל במזיד קידש — דר"מ לטעמיה, דאמר: הקדש במזיד מתחלל. ומפיק לה מקרא (או מעלה מעל), ואין מעילה אלא בשינוי, כלומר במזיד, דאם ירצה לגוזלו יקננו מיד; וזה שינה היכא דקידש במזיד. וראיה ד"מעלה מעל" הוי במזיד — דכתיב (במדבר ה׳:י״ב) גבי סוטה, גבי "איש כי תשטה אשתו": "ומעלה בו מעל", והתם על כרחך במזיד קאמר, דודאי כשמזנה מזידה היא. וקרא ד"ונתן הכסף וקם לו" — למצוה בעלמא, דבלאו כסף הוא מתחלל אם ירצה לגוזלו. ומיהו במעשר קאמר רבי מאיר דבין בשוגג ובין במזיד לא קידש — דבמעילה הוא דגלי קרא דבמזיד מתחלל, אבל מעשר — דכל היכא דאיתא, שם מעשר עליו. ורבי יהודה סבר: ממון בעלים הוא, ולכך במזיד קידש — דממונא הוא, אבל בשוגג לא — משום טירחא דאורחא:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 53b:6:1.english: "Even with regard to a sale he does not acquire" - And the money does not become desacralized. And me'ilah [misuse of consecrated property] applies according to Rabbi Meir only to one who eats consecrated food, but regarding one who spends consecrated [money], he does not incur me'ilah, for wherever it is, the status of consecration applies to it; for wherever it is, it is in the treasury of the Merciful One, since had he known [it was consecrated], he would not have spent it. But [if he betrothed her] intentionally, she is betrothed, as Rabbi Meir follows his [standard] reasoning, as he says: Consecrated property becomes desacralized [when misused] intentionally. And he derives this from the verse (or: "me'alah ma'al"), [which teaches that] me'ilah is only through an alteration [in status] — that is, intentionally — for if he wishes to steal it, he acquires it immediately, and this person effected an alteration where he betrothed [her] intentionally. And proof that "me'alah ma'al" refers to [an action done] intentionally is that it is written regarding a sotah (Numbers 5:12), regarding "if any man's wife goes astray": "and commit a trespass [u-ma'alah vo ma'al] against him" — and there, perforce it is speaking of [an act done] intentionally, for certainly when she commits adultery, she acts intentionally. And the verse [which states], "and he shall give the money and it shall be assured to him" [Leviticus 27:19], is merely for a mitzvah [as the prescribed procedure], for without money it becomes desacralized if he wishes to steal it. However, regarding [second] tithe, Rabbi Meir says that whether unwittingly or intentionally, she is not betrothed, for it is only regarding me'ilah that the verse revealed that it becomes desacralized intentionally; but regarding tithe, wherever it is, the status of tithe remains upon it. And Rabbi Yehuda holds that it is the owner's property, and therefore [if he betrothed her] intentionally, she is betrothed, as it is monetary property; but unwittingly, [she is] not, due to the burden of the journey.
